assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Sai Life Sciences (consolidated, Rs crore). Sai reports one segment but discloses CDMO (development and manufacturing; deck basis incl. other operating income) and CRO (discovery) revenue; the engine runs one revenue-growth path and the two-line build sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/SAILIFE.ctx.js. EBITDA on Screener's basis (forex in other income; the company's own EBITDA includes forex). Other income and interest are built in SAILIFE.ctx.js from sourced parts and written here by SAILIFE.mult.js. Valued on EV/EBITDA, the method all brokers that disclose one use.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two-line build below. FY27 +16.8%: Q1FY27 revenue +12% (CRO +24%, CDMO +6%); management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 as the first 225 KL block at Bidar starts in H2/Q3 and says it has over 90% visibility on FY27 targets; production started on 3 of the 4 commercial molecules added last year. FY27 needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs2,007 cr, +18% on Rs1,695 cr a year earlier. FY28 +19.0% / FY29 +17.6%: both 225 KL blocks run (capacity ~1,150 KL), 14 late-phase molecules (two regulatory milestones in FY27, one in Q2FY28) convert to commercial supply, FTE contracts with large pharma scale. Guidance: 15-20% a year over three to five years. Street: HDFC Securities FY27E Rs2,551 cr / FY28E Rs3,036 cr (Jan-2026); Jefferies 17% sales CAGR FY26-28 (Mar-2026).

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs2,192 cr: CDMO Rs1,417 cr (+33%) and CRO Rs775 cr (+24%) on the deck basis (Q4FY26 deck p.11); the audited note shows CDMO contract revenue Rs1,361.5 cr and CRO Rs775.4 cr, with Rs55.7 cr of other operating income (solvent sales, government incentives) that the deck adds to CDMO.

businessLines._why: CDMO +14% in FY27: Q1 +6% on campaign timing; H2 lifted by the first new Bidar block and three new commercial molecules in production (two of them as primary supplier); FY26's +33% was helped by recovery from FY25 destocking. +19% / +18% in FY28-29 as the second block fills, late-phase molecules convert and the large-pharma FTE engagements (five of the last six late-phase additions) move into supply. CRO +22% in FY27 (Q1 +24%; a discovery facility opened in Q1 is already sold out; a pilot converted into a long-term high-volume partnership), easing to +19% / +17% as the base grows (discovery revenue grew ~30-35% a year over four to five years, CFO).

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (forex gains in other income): 19.6% (FY24), 24.2% (FY25), 28.9% (FY26), 26.7% in Q1FY27. FY26 was flattered by a Rs34 cr provision reversal (~1.2 points; FY25 depressed by the original provision). Company guidance is 28-30% over two to three years on its own basis, which includes forex (FY26 company 30.1%, of which forex ~1.4 points); management warns of near-term inefficiencies from new capacity. FY27 28.0%: material margin ~74%, people cost ~31% of sales, new blocks and formulation/peptide labs before revenue. FY28 28.5% and FY29 29.0%: operating leverage as utilisation rises from 65%. Street: HDFC Securities 28.1% FY27E, 29.1% FY28E.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs633 cr (company; budget Rs700 cr). FY27 guidance Rs1,100-1,300 cr (~75% capacity, ~25% capability), reiterated on 7-Aug-2026; Rs263 cr spent in Q1. FY28 not guided: we assume Rs900 cr for the Choutuppal greenfield (~1,400 KL planned; commercial peptide plant by 2028; peptide spend under Rs300 cr to 2028) and the second Bidar block; FY29 Rs700 cr. Capital commitments Rs354 cr at Mar-26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs167 cr (incl. Rs47 cr on lease assets) = 7.1% of average Screener gross block; Q1FY27 Rs46 cr (Rs184 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex in the year it is spent (CWIP held flat), but much of FY27-28 capex sits in CWIP (Choutuppal, peptide plant) until 2028, so we use 6.0%: ~Rs192 / 255 / 303 cr in FY27-29E. HDFC Securities FY27E Rs191 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is built in SAILIFE.ctx.js on the gross cash and deposits Sai keeps (the engine's net figure turns into net debt as capex is borrowed) and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (checked in SAILIFE.ctx.js): (1) interest on cash, deposits and funds at 4.74%, the yield Sai realised in FY26 (deposit interest Rs18.48 cr on average gross treasury of ~Rs390 cr: Rs508 cr at Mar-25 incl. unspent IPO money, Rs273 cr at Mar-26), applied to the gross cash and deposits we assume Sai keeps (Rs273 cr at Mar-26, ~Rs200 cr thereafter, borrowing the rest of its capex); (2) other small items Rs0.5 cr (FY26 Rs0.9 cr). No forex gains forecast (FY26 Rs29.8 cr, FY25 Rs19.1 cr; the company reports them inside EBITDA). Government incentives (Rs31.3 cr in FY26) are revenue, not other income. FY26 other income Rs49.1 cr incl. forex (Screener, net of the Rs9.0 cr exceptional: Rs40.2 cr); Q1FY27 Rs3.5 cr (Rs14 cr annualised) as the IPO cash was spent.

otherTreasury._why: Fixed deposits with financial institutions (Rs47.5 cr non-current, Rs60.0 cr current) and margin-money deposits (Rs4.0 cr) at Mar-26 sit in other financial assets (AR FY26 note 10), inside Screener's Other Assets. They are treasury; the engine and the Excel take them out of working capital and add them to net cash.

assumptions._interestWhy: Built in SAILIFE.ctx.js: 8.5% on average bank debt (Rs95 -> 743 -> 1090 -> 1119 cr, Mar-26 to Mar-29E: the engine's net debt plus the ~Rs200 cr of gross cash less Rs193 cr of leases; AA-rated borrower) plus lease interest at FY26's 11.1% on Rs193 cr of lease liabilities (Rs21.5 cr) plus ~Rs3 cr of other finance costs. FY26 finance cost Rs39.2 cr (borrowings Rs11.0 cr, leases Rs23.2 cr, other Rs5.0 cr); Q1FY27 Rs8 cr. Capitalised interest during construction (nil in FY26) is not assumed.
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend declared since listing (FY25-26 payout nil); FY27-29 capex exceeds operating cash flow, so we assume none.

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 1.0 (12.5% cost of equity). Net debt stays modest relative to market value, so WACC is close to the cost of equity; the engine discounts at the cost of equity. Revenue is lumpy (Q1FY27 CDMO +6%) but spread over 300+ customers.
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: Indian CRDMO is forecast to grow 15-16% a year to CY2035 (AR FY26 MD&A) and outsourcing keeps rising.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% (FY29E) to 8% by FY42E; revenue grew ~24% a year in FY21-26 (Rs760 cr to Rs2,192 cr).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 28%, below our FY29E 29%: larger commercial volumes carry tighter pricing and new modalities start at lower margins.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~47% / 30% / 20% of sales (FY27-29E) to 8% by FY42E: maintenance (~7% of sales; FY26 depreciation 7.6% incl. leases) plus growth capex at Sai's ~0.85x gross asset turn.
dcf._wcNote: Operating working capital is ~19% of FY26 sales on Screener's Mar-26 balance sheet (other assets less cash and deposits, less other liabilities incl. capex creditors); the engine holds it at that level.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Late-phase molecules convert on time, the large-pharma FTE engagements turn into commercial supply and both Bidar blocks fill quickly; growth runs ~4 points a year faster and the margin reaches the top of the 28-30% guide.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A repeat of FY25: a large customer destocks and CDMO stalls while the new capacity and its people are already paid for; growth slows ~6 points a year and the margin falls back towards FY25's 24-25%.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Sai Life: all three brokers that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA (HDFC Securities 29x Q3FY28E, Jan-2026; JM Financial 32x Sep-27E, Nov-2025; Jefferies initiated on 27x FY27 pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA, Mar-2025); Kotak and Morgan Stanley targets come without a method. 29x = Sai's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Jul-2025 (listed 18-Dec-2024; IPO months skipped; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 66 points; EV = market value less the last published net cash incl. deposits and leases; forward EBITDA = our FY27E/FY28E, which carry no exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 26.8x x 1.091 (nine pharma peers' trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +9.1%) = 29.2x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash (negative: net debt incl. leases). Bull 32.5x / bear 27.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (29.7x / 25.2x) x 1.091. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by SAILIFE.mult.js.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check: Sai's median one-year-forward P/E since 1-Jul-2025 (same weekly closes; forward EPS = our FY27E/FY28E) of 54.7x x 1.185 (the nine peers' P/E move over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +18.5%) = 64.8x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 78.5x / bear 61.5x = 75th / 25th percentile x 1.185.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity; modest net debt), terminal growth 6%, plus net cash at Mar-27.

cover.headline: A good integrated CRDMO priced for a re-rating the sector has not had: on Sai Life's own forward EV/EBITDA and the pharma sector's move the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}}, a SELL
cover.lead: Sai Life Sciences discovers molecules for drug innovators (CRO, 35% of FY26 revenue of ₹2,192 cr) and develops and makes them (CDMO, 65%), almost all for export and mostly for large pharma: 19 of the top 25 are clients, repeat customers bring over 90% of revenue and no customer is above ~12%. Q1FY27 revenue rose 12% (CRO +24%, CDMO +6%) and management guides 15-20% growth a year with a stronger H2. We forecast EBITDA in line with the street but EPS of only ₹16.8 / 18.4 / 22.2 for FY27-29E, well below it, because capex doubles to ₹1,100-1,300 cr in FY27 and is funded with debt. Every broker that discloses a method uses **EV/EBITDA**, and so do we: Sai's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since Jul-2025 (26.8x), lifted 9.1% for the pharma sector's move over the same window, gives **29x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹954 cr less net debt = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL**. Cross-checks: P/E ₹1,318; DCF ₹418. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A real franchise with large pharma
arguments.p: An integrated discovery-to-commercial platform; 33 commercial and 14 late-phase molecules; five of six recent late-phase additions came through dedicated large-pharma teams; a clean USFDA/PMDA record; the margin rebuilt from 14% (FY23) to 29% (FY26).

arguments.h: But the next three years are capex-heavy
arguments.p: ₹2,800 cr of capex in FY27-29E against ~₹1,700 cr in the previous six years; net debt goes from ~₹16 cr to ~₹1,112 cr (incl. leases). EBITDA grows ~18% a year; EPS only ~10%. HDFC Securities' FY28E EPS (₹23.6) was set before the capex guide doubled.

arguments.h: FY26 looked better than the run-rate
arguments.p: A ₹34 cr provision reversal and ₹30 cr of forex gains helped FY26; the underlying company margin was ~27.5%, Q1FY27 26.7%. CDMO growth slowed to 6% in Q1 and management will not guide by business.

arguments.h: The price has outrun the history and the sector
arguments.p: ₹1,525 is 37.2x our FY28E EBITDA and 89.0x trailing EPS; Sai's EV/EBITDA is +36.1% above its own median since Jul-2025 while the pharma set is +9.1%. The DCF needs ~26% growth for 15 years. The rule says SELL above ~₹1,320.

sections.title: A Hyderabad CRDMO that discovers molecules for innovators (CRO, 35% of revenue) and develops and makes them (CDMO, 65%); 99% of revenue is exported

blocks.p: Sai Life is a CRDMO: a contract research, development and manufacturing organisation for drug innovators. It does two things. (1) **Discovery (CRO)**: medicinal and synthetic chemistry, biology, DMPK (how a drug is absorbed and cleared) and toxicology that help a client find a drug candidate and file it for human trials, sold mostly by the scientist-year (FTE) or by project from its Hyderabad campus and labs in Greater Boston. (2) **Development and manufacturing (CDMO, which Sai calls CMC)**: designing the chemical process, making material for Phase I-III trials and then supplying the active ingredient (API) or advanced intermediates for approved drugs from 700 KL of reactors at Bidar, with process R&D in Hyderabad and Manchester. It works almost only in small molecules, with early work in peptides, ADC payloads and linkers and oligonucleotide building blocks (~4% of revenue). FY26 revenue was ₹2,192 cr: CDMO ₹1,417 cr (+33%) and CRO ₹775 cr (+24%); 99.4% came from outside India. It has 3,806 employees, 2,000+ of them in R&D.

blocks.callout: **So what:** Sai is closer to a large-pharma supplier than a biotech-funded CRO. The discovery business wins relationships early; the CDMO business earns from them once a molecule reaches late trials or the market. That model is why repeat customers bring over 90% of revenue and no customer is more than ~12% of sales. It also means growth follows a few dozen molecules and campaign timing, which makes quarters lumpy.

sections.title: Twenty-seven years from a chemistry shop to a listed CRDMO; the IPO raised ₹950 cr to repay debt, and TPG sold out within nine months of listing

blocks.p: The Kanumuri family founded Sai in Hyderabad in 1999 as a medicinal-chemistry partner to US biotechs. It pivoted to manufacturing in 2009-13 (Unit IV at Bidar won its first USFDA approval), added process R&D and integrated biology, and in 2019-23 opened labs in Manchester and Greater Boston and built HPAPI, clean-room and amidite blocks at Bidar. TPG became the largest outside investor before the IPO. The heavy investment of FY19-FY23 came with thin profits and rising debt (₹933 cr at Mar-23), which the IPO repaid.

blocks.h: The IPO: ₹3,043 cr, of which ₹950 cr was new money

blocks.p: Sai listed on 18-Dec-2024 at ₹549 a share (a ~20% listing gain). It issued 1.73 cr new shares for ₹950 cr and selling shareholders sold 3.81 cr shares for ₹2,093 cr. Net proceeds of ₹910 cr went to repaying ₹720 cr of borrowings and ₹190 cr of general corporate purposes, all used by Mar-2026. Offer expenses (₹128 cr) were split pro rata, and the company's share was charged to securities premium, not profit. The ESOP charge was only ₹2-3 cr a year in FY24-FY26, so the IPO left no one-off in the P&L to adjust. TPG then sold ~10% on 20-Jun-2025 at ~₹722 and its last 14.72% on 26-Aug-2025 at ~₹871; Nippon India MF, Invesco MF, BlackRock and Societe Generale were among the buyers.

blocks.callout: **Lesson from history:** Sai has been here before. In FY20-FY23 it built capacity and people ahead of revenue and profit almost disappeared (FY22 PAT ₹6 cr). The FY27-29 capex cycle is larger (₹1,100-1,300 cr in FY27 alone) but starts from a healthier base: 29% margins, a full order book and an AA balance sheet. The risk is the same: costs arrive before revenue.

sections.title: Industry: India's CRDMO market is ~USD3.4-4.0 bn and forecast to grow 15-16% a year to 2035, faster than the world's 8-9%; Sai is one of a handful of scaled integrated players

blocks.p: Sai's annual report cites a global CDMO market of ~USD 214.95 bn in 2026 growing 8.7% a year to ~USD 419.93 bn by 2034, and a global CRO (research) market of USD 45.3 bn in 2025 growing ~8% a year. India's CRDMO market is estimated at USD 3.4-4 bn in CY2025 and forecast to grow 15-16% a year to USD 7-9 bn by CY2030 and USD 14-18 bn by CY2035. Sai's FY26 revenue of ~USD 0.25 bn is ~7% of that Indian market. The same report flags the near term honestly: CRDMO revenue growth of 8-10% in FY27 because biopharma funding has been weak. The long-term drivers: innovators outsource more, large pharma wants integrated partners outside China, new modalities need specialist capacity, and patent expiries push innovators to cut costs.

sections.title: Discovery: the steadier engine, +24% in FY26 and Q1FY27, increasingly integrated and increasingly large pharma

blocks.p: Discovery revenue was ₹775 cr in FY26 (+24%) and ~₹222 cr in Q1FY27 (+24%). The CFO says it has compounded at ~30-35% a year over four to five years, helped by the Boston lab, which meets biotechs "even before they actually have a need" for an Indian partner. Sai sells integrated programmes (chemistry, biology, DMPK and toxicology together) to ~65% of its discovery customers; in Q1FY27 a pilot with a large pharma became "a long-term, high-volume discovery chemistry partnership" and management hopes to move two large pharmas to integrated models in FY27. A new discovery facility opened in Q1FY27 was sold out at once, and a 100,000 sq ft R&D building opened at Genome Valley. On our reading of the deck, pharma's share of discovery revenue rose from ~38% to ~48% in FY26.

sections.title: CDMO: 33 commercial and 14 late-phase molecules for large pharma; growth comes in campaigns, and Q1FY27 was a slow one

blocks.p: CDMO revenue was ₹1,417 cr in FY26 (+33%; ₹1,361 cr of contract revenue plus ₹56 cr of solvent sales and government incentives) and ~₹332 cr in Q1FY27 (+6%). The portfolio at Mar-26: 34 commercial molecules, 11 in Phase III or pre-registration and 155 programmes in early development; by Jun-26, 33 and 14. Sai supported 17 launches in five years and five FDA-approved drugs in CY2025. HDFC Securities counts 38 APIs and intermediates for 28 commercial drugs, seven of them blockbusters. The pipeline now grows three ways (CEO): biotech clients acquired by pharma partners keep their molecules with Sai, pharma moves acquired molecules to Sai as a preferred vendor, and dedicated FTE development teams carry molecules into late phase. Five of the six late-phase molecules added in the last 15 months came from FTE relationships, one of which now runs from discovery to commercial.

blocks.h: Customers: concentrated by campaign, not by name

blocks.p: No customer is very large. One customer paid ₹267 cr (12.2% of revenue) in FY26; in FY25 two customers paid ₹364 cr (21.5%), and in FY24 none passed 10%. Returning customers brought over 90% of revenue in FY25 and FY26, and the average large-pharma relationship is 11+ years old. Concentration shows up instead in timing: a commercial customer's destocking turned Q1FY25 into a loss quarter and forced a provision on an early intermediate (₹34 cr of it reversed in FY26 when orders resumed). Sai names none of its customers or molecules.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** the CDMO funnel is healthier than one slow quarter suggests (14 late-phase molecules, FTE-fed), and customer risk is lower than at most Indian CDMOs. But CDMO revenue moves with a few campaigns and Sai will not guide by business. We model +14% in FY27 (H2-weighted as the Bidar block starts) and +19% / +18% in FY28-29 as late-phase molecules convert.

sections.title: Capacity: 700 KL to ~1,150 KL by end-FY27 and a ~1,400 KL greenfield after; capex doubles to ₹1,100-1,300 cr in FY27

blocks.p: Sai's manufacturing capacity went from 200 KL in 2017 to 526 KL in FY25 and ~700 KL by Sep-2025 (80 production trains at Bidar, reactors of 0.25-12 KL, an HPAPI block). Two more 225 KL production blocks (450 KL) are being built at Bidar; the first starts in H2/Q3FY27 and management expects ~1,150 KL by end-FY27. Utilisation was 65% in Q1FY27. Beyond that, Sai has bought ~40 acres at Choutuppal near Hyderabad for a greenfield site designed for ~1,400 KL plus development, warehousing and QC, where a commercial peptide plant should run from 2028 (peptide spend under ₹300 cr). On the research side, a discovery block opened in Q1FY27 (already full), a 100,000 sq ft R&D facility opened at Genome Valley, a new process R&D block doubles PRD capacity, and an XDC centre and a clinical formulation unit are coming.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: real in integration, large-pharma relationships and regulatory record; weak in scale and new modalities

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. Sai has a narrow one. It comes from being embedded with large pharma early (discovery and FTE development teams) and staying with a molecule through approval, backed by a clean inspection record. Customers rarely switch a filed supplier. What Sai lacks is scale (700 KL of reactors against several thousand at Divi's or Laurus), any biologics capability, and returns that clearly beat its cost of capital: ROE was 14% and ROCE 18% in FY26 against a ~12.5% cost of equity. Syngene, Anthem, Aragen, Cohance, Divi's and Laurus in India, and WuXi and other Chinese CDMOs, chase the same pharma work.

blocks.callout: **Verdict:** a genuine but narrow moat. Integration and large-pharma trust explain why Sai keeps 90%+ of revenue from repeat customers and why its margin has rebuilt to ~29%. sections.title: Quality and regulatory record: USFDA and PMDA inspections cleared across sites, no warning letter; one new environmental PIL at Bidar

blocks.p: For a contract manufacturer the regulatory record is the licence to operate. Sai says it has a "100% successful track record" in regulatory inspections across its R&D and manufacturing sites: USFDA, Japan's PMDA and Mexico's COFEPRIS, plus EMA audits and more than 30 PSCI (pharma supply-chain) audits in seven years. We found no warning letter, import alert or recall in the filings. The quality team (300+ QA/QC staff) reports to the CEO. The new Bidar blocks and the Choutuppal site will need their own inspections as commercial products move in.

blocks.p: Sai ships development and commercial campaigns, so a quarter rises or falls with a few deliveries. Management says the business has historically split 40/60 between the first and second halves; FY26 was an exception at 48/52 after a strong H1. In Q1FY25 revenue fell to ₹280 cr as a commercial customer destocked, and the quarter made a loss; in Q3FY26 the margin reached 34% on a rich mix. Q1FY27 revenue rose 12% to ₹554 cr with CDMO only +6%; management expects H2FY27 to be stronger as the first new 225 KL production block at Bidar starts. sections.title: Revenue ×3 in seven years; margins collapsed in FY22-23 and have rebuilt to 29%; profit only became meaningful in FY25-26

blocks.p: Sai Life grew revenue from ₹695 cr in FY19 to ₹2,192 cr in FY26, 23.6% a year over the last five years. The path had two halves. In FY19-FY23 revenue grew but profit shrank: the EBITDA margin (Screener basis, forex in other income) fell from 25% to 14% as Sai hired scientists, built biology and DMPK labs, opened Boston and Manchester and added manufacturing blocks ahead of demand, and interest on ₹750-930 cr of debt ate what was left (FY22 net profit ₹6 cr, FY23 ₹10 cr). In FY24-FY26 the investment paid off: revenue +20%, +16% and +29%, margin 19.6% → 24.2% → 28.9%, and the IPO money (₹950 cr, Dec-2024) repaid ₹720 cr of debt, halving interest. Net profit went ₹83 cr → ₹170 cr → ₹349 cr. FY26 had help: a ₹34 cr reversal of a FY25 provision and ₹30 cr of forex gains.

sections.title: From ₹930 cr of debt to roughly net debt-free after the IPO, and back to borrowing: we see net debt of ~₹1,100 cr by Mar-28 as capex doubles

blocks.p: Sai carried ₹750-930 cr of borrowings in FY22-24 while it built capacity on thin profits. The IPO's ₹950 cr fresh issue (Dec-2024) repaid ₹720 cr of it. At Mar-26 Sai had ₹273 cr of cash, deposits and funds (₹111 cr of cash and bank balances, ₹51 cr of investments and ₹112 cr of fixed deposits held in other financial assets) against ₹95 cr of bank debt and ₹194 cr of lease liabilities: net debt including leases of ~₹16 cr, net debt/equity 0.01. That position is now reversing. FY26 capex of ₹633 cr already used most of the IPO cash (₹464 cr of cash at Mar-25 became ₹111 cr), and FY27 capex is guided at ₹1,100-1,300 cr against operating cash flow of ~₹500 cr. Receivables are well run (62 days in FY26), but contract assets and other current assets (₹624 cr) have grown with revenue recognised over time.

blocks.h: How the street values Sai Life

blocks.p: Every broker that discloses a method values Sai on **EV/EBITDA**: HDFC Securities (29x Q3FY28E), JM Financial (32x Sep-27E in Nov-2025) and Jefferies (27x FY27 pre-Ind AS EBITDA at initiation; later multiples not disclosed in the sources we read). Kotak and Morgan Stanley targets came without a method. We follow the street: **EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E, half FY29E)**, the year a buyer will look at one year from now, plus Sep-28E net cash (negative here: ₹1,098 cr of net debt including ₹193 cr of leases, consistent with EBITDA after Ind AS 116 lease costs). EV/EBITDA also suits Sai better than P/E during a capex cycle, because it is not distorted by depreciation and interest that rise before the new capacity earns. P/E and a DCF are cross-checks.

Sai listed on 18-Dec-2024, so it has 21 months of history, not five years. Following the batch rule (PLAYBOOK §7c, as for EMCURE and MANKIND), we skip the first six months after listing and use its one-year-forward EV/EBITDA **since 1-Jul-2025**, on every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (66 points): market value less the last published net cash (incl. deposits and leases), divided by the next full fiscal year's EBITDA, which is our FY27E (₹717 cr) for dates to Mar-2026 and our FY28E (₹869 cr) after. Our forecasts carry no exceptional items, and Sai's history has none worth adjusting (the FY26 labour-code charge was ₹9 cr; IPO costs went to securities premium; the ESOP charge is ₹2-3 cr a year), so the median before exceptional items and on reported numbers is the same. No forward year is a trough (EPS rises every year). We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' EV/EBITDA move over the **same window** (+9.1%) and round to the nearest half-turn. Sai's own move, growth and returns do not enter the base; they are sensitivities below.

assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two-line build below. FY27 +16.8%: Q1FY27 revenue +12% (CRO +24%, CDMO +6%); management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 as the first 225 KL block at Bidar starts in H2/Q3 and says it has over 90% visibility on FY27 targets; production started on 3 of the 4 commercial molecules added last year. FY27 needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs2,007 cr, +18% on Rs1,695 cr a year earlier. FY28 +19.0% / FY29 +17.6%: both 225 KL blocks run (capacity ~1,150 KL), 14 late-phase molecules (two regulatory milestones in FY27, one in Q2FY28) convert to commercial supply, FTE contracts with large pharma scale. Guidance: 15-20% a year over three to five years. Street: HDFC Securities FY27E Rs2,551 cr / FY28E Rs3,036 cr (Jan-2026); Jefferies 17% sales CAGR FY26-28 (Mar-2026).

base._why: FY26 revenue Rs2,192 cr: CDMO Rs1,417 cr (+33%) and CRO Rs775 cr (+24%) on the deck basis (Q4FY26 deck p.11); the audited note shows CDMO contract revenue Rs1,361.5 cr and CRO Rs775.4 cr, with Rs55.7 cr of other operating income (solvent sales, government incentives) that the deck adds to CDMO.

businessLines._why: CDMO +14% in FY27: Q1 +6% on campaign timing; H2 lifted by the first new Bidar block and three new commercial molecules in production (two of them as primary supplier); FY26's +33% was helped by recovery from FY25 destocking. +19% / +18% in FY28-29 as the second block fills, late-phase molecules convert and the large-pharma FTE engagements (five of the last six late-phase additions) move into supply. CRO +22% in FY27 (Q1 +24%; a discovery facility opened in Q1 is already sold out; a pilot converted into a long-term high-volume partnership), easing to +19% / +17% as the base grows (discovery revenue grew ~30-35% a year over four to five years, CFO).

assumptions._marginWhy: Screener basis (forex gains in other income): 19.6% (FY24), 24.2% (FY25), 28.9% (FY26), 26.7% in Q1FY27. FY26 was flattered by a Rs34 cr provision reversal (~1.2 points; FY25 depressed by the original provision). Company guidance is 28-30% over two to three years on its own basis, which includes forex (FY26 company 30.1%, of which forex ~1.4 points); management warns of near-term inefficiencies from new capacity. FY27 28.0%: material margin ~74%, people cost ~31% of sales, new blocks and formulation/peptide labs before revenue. FY28 28.5% and FY29 29.0%: operating leverage as utilisation rises from 65%. Street: HDFC Securities 28.1% FY27E, 29.1% FY28E.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 capex Rs633 cr (company; budget Rs700 cr). FY27 guidance Rs1,100-1,300 cr (~75% capacity, ~25% capability), reiterated on 7-Aug-2026; Rs263 cr spent in Q1. FY28 not guided: we assume Rs900 cr for the Choutuppal greenfield (~1,400 KL planned; commercial peptide plant by 2028; peptide spend under Rs300 cr to 2028) and the second Bidar block; FY29 Rs700 cr. Capital commitments Rs354 cr at Mar-26.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs167 cr (incl. Rs47 cr on lease assets) = 7.1% of average Screener gross block; Q1FY27 Rs46 cr (Rs184 cr annualised). The engine depreciates capex in the year it is spent (CWIP held flat), but much of FY27-28 capex sits in CWIP (Choutuppal, peptide plant) until 2028, so we use 6.0%: ~Rs192 / 255 / 303 cr in FY27-29E. HDFC Securities FY27E Rs191 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury income is built in SAILIFE.ctx.js on the gross cash and deposits Sai keeps (the engine's net figure turns into net debt as capex is borrowed) and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (checked in SAILIFE.ctx.js): (1) interest on cash, deposits and funds at 4.74%, the yield Sai realised in FY26 (deposit interest Rs18.48 cr on average gross treasury of ~Rs390 cr: Rs508 cr at Mar-25 incl. unspent IPO money, Rs273 cr at Mar-26), applied to the gross cash and deposits we assume Sai keeps (Rs273 cr at Mar-26, ~Rs200 cr thereafter, borrowing the rest of its capex); (2) other small items Rs0.5 cr (FY26 Rs0.9 cr). No forex gains forecast (FY26 Rs29.8 cr, FY25 Rs19.1 cr; the company reports them inside EBITDA). Government incentives (Rs31.3 cr in FY26) are revenue, not other income. FY26 other income Rs49.1 cr incl. forex (Screener, net of the Rs9.0 cr exceptional: Rs40.2 cr); Q1FY27 Rs3.5 cr (Rs14 cr annualised) as the IPO cash was spent.

otherTreasury._why: Fixed deposits with financial institutions (Rs47.5 cr non-current, Rs60.0 cr current) and margin-money deposits (Rs4.0 cr) at Mar-26 sit in other financial assets (AR FY26 note 10), inside Screener's Other Assets. They are treasury; the engine and the Excel take them out of working capital and add them to net cash.

assumptions._interestWhy: Built in SAILIFE.ctx.js: 8.5% on average bank debt (Rs95 -> 743 -> 1090 -> 1119 cr, Mar-26 to Mar-29E: the engine's net debt plus the ~Rs200 cr of gross cash less Rs193 cr of leases; AA-rated borrower) plus lease interest at FY26's 11.1% on Rs193 cr of lease liabilities (Rs21.5 cr) plus ~Rs3 cr of other finance costs. assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend declared since listing (FY25-26 payout nil); FY27-29 capex exceeds operating cash flow, so we assume none.

dcf._betaWhy: Beta 1.0 (12.5% cost of equity). Net debt stays modest relative to market value, so WACC is close to the cost of equity; the engine discounts at the cost of equity. Revenue is lumpy (Q1FY27 CDMO +6%) but spread over 300+ customers.
dcf._tgWhy: Top of the house 5-6% range: Indian CRDMO is forecast to grow 15-16% a year to CY2035 (AR FY26 MD&A) and outsourcing keeps rising.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~18% (FY29E) to 8% by FY42E; revenue grew ~24% a year in FY21-26 (Rs760 cr to Rs2,192 cr).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 28%, below our FY29E 29%: larger commercial volumes carry tighter pricing and new modalities start at lower margins.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~47% / 30% / 20% of sales (FY27-29E) to 8% by FY42E: maintenance (~7% of sales; FY26 depreciation 7.6% incl. leases) plus growth capex at Sai's ~0.85x gross asset turn.

primary.why: How the street values Sai Life: all three brokers that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA (HDFC Securities 29x Q3FY28E, Jan-2026; JM Financial 32x Sep-27E, Nov-2025; Jefferies initiated on 27x FY27 pre-Ind AS EV/EBITDA, Mar-2025); Kotak and Morgan Stanley targets come without a method. 29x = Sai's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Jul-2025 (listed 18-Dec-2024; IPO months skipped; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 66 points; EV = market value less the last published net cash incl. deposits and leases; forward EBITDA = our FY27E/FY28E, which carry no exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 26.8x x 1.091 (nine pharma peers' trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced +9.1%) = 29.2x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net cash (negative: net debt incl. leases). Bull 32.5x / bear 27.5x = 75th / 25th percentile (29.7x / 25.2x) x 1.091. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by SAILIFE.mult.js.
